One who does not believe in the existence of God
Atheist = one who does not believe in God (a- = without, theos = god). A theist believes in God; an agnostic says God's existence cannot be known.
A person who loves and collects books
Bibliophile = lover of books (biblio = book, phile = lover). Philatelist collects stamps, numismatist collects coins, oenophile loves wine.
Misogynist = one who hates women (miso = hate, gyne = woman). Misanthrope hates mankind; misogamist hates marriage; philanthropist loves mankind.
A person who can speak many languages
Polyglot = one who knows many languages (poly = many, glotta = tongue). Bilingual means two languages only; an orator is a skilled public speaker.
The life story of a person written by himself or herself
Autobiography = life story written by oneself (auto = self). A biography is written by someone else; an anthology is a collection of writings.
Happening or published after a person's death
Posthumous = occurring or published after death, e.g. a posthumous award. Anonymous = name not known; unanimous = everyone agrees.
A child who has lost both parents
Orphan = a child who has lost both parents. A widow has lost her husband; a bachelor is an unmarried man; an heir inherits property.
A person who is unable to pay his or her debts
Insolvent = unable to pay debts. Do not mix up: indolent = lazy, insolent = rude, ignorant = lacking knowledge.
Omniscient = all-knowing (omni = all, scient = knowing). Omnipotent = all-powerful; omnipresent = present everywhere; omnivorous = eating everything.
A sentimental longing for the past
Nostalgia = sentimental longing for the past (nostos = return home, algos = pain). Neuralgia = nerve pain; amnesia = memory loss; insomnia = sleeplessness.
